searchText: Quick question on the Gloas getPayload timeout in Prysm. I heard it was raised to 600ms, but on develop engine_getPayloadV6 still has a 300ms deadline (from #17212): https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/c4e939f38dc8ae798b3938853c2aefef82b8dcba/beacon-chain/execution/engine_jsonrpc.go#L117-L118 The only 600ms change I found is #17551, which raises the builder bid wait, but not the EL call. The spec sets a 1s timeout for engine_getPayloadV6: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/main/src/engine/amsterdam.md#engine_getpayloadv6 https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/main/src/engine/common.md#timeouts Can we either change the spec or the values in Prysm? The problem is in Besu when we get a getPayload request and only have an empty block ready, we wait up to 800ms to build a better one, with Prysm we can miss a block because of that. We chose the 800ms because according to the spec that should be fine. We can reduce our waiting time on our side if needed, but it would be great if we can decide first what the timeout in the spec actually should be. yes, we didn't think the engine could need more than 300ms to seal a block locally, given that we are asking the external builder over an internet connection to do it on 600ms. Should we revisit this deadline? At any rate, yes, a 1 second wait in the spec is just ridiculous cc <@425572898787426305> but also, Besu's behavior of waiting 800ms to seal a better block is also incorrect IMO, you should deliver an empty one I believe. would you mind opening a PR with whatever number you think is reasonable? I think 1s was there since Paris I can look at local benchmarks and open one i guess 6s for `newPayload` is fine, isn't it? Hello. Running some local devnets with heze-devnet-2, we found that Lighthouse sometimes defaults to an empty IL view at the first slot of an epoch. We made a PR here: https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/pull/10436

excerpts.author: daniellehrner
excerpts.content:
Quick question on the Gloas getPayload timeout in Prysm. I heard it was raised to 600ms, but on develop engine_getPayloadV6 still has a 300ms deadline (from #17212):
https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/c4e939f38dc8ae798b3938853c2aefef82b8dcba/beacon-chain/execution/engine_jsonrpc.go#L117-L118

The only 600ms change I found is #17551, which raises the builder bid wait, but not the EL call.

The spec sets a 1s timeout for engine_getPayloadV6:
https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/main/src/engine/amsterdam.md#engine_getpayloadv6
https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/main/src/engine/common.md#timeouts

Can we either change the spec or the values in Prysm? The problem is in Besu when we get a getPayload request and only have an empty block ready, we wait up to 800ms to build a better one, with Prysm we can miss a block because of that. We chose the 800ms because according to the spec that should be fine. We can reduce our waiting time on our side if needed, but it would be great if we can decide first what the timeout in the spec actually should be.

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: yes, we didn't think the engine could need more than 300ms to seal a block locally, given that we are asking the external builder over an internet connection to do it on 600ms. Should we revisit this deadline?

excerpts.content: At any rate, yes, a 1 second wait in the spec is just ridiculous cc <@425572898787426305> but also, Besu's behavior of waiting 800ms to seal a better block is also incorrect IMO, you should deliver an empty one I believe.
